questions.question: Why must breaking changes (feat!:) be in their own changelog section?
choices: They represent backward-incompatible changes that can break existing code — users need to see them first
questions.explanation: Breaking changes can cause existing code to fail when users upgrade. Putting them in a prominent, separate section ensures developers see them immediately and can prepare for the impact.

questions.question: After categorizing a commit by its prefix, what should happen to the prefix in the display message?
choices: Strip it: 'add user profile' (the section heading already shows the type)
Move it to the end: 'add user profile (feat)'
questions.explanation: Once you've placed a commit in the correct section (e.g., ## Features), the type prefix is redundant in the display message. Show just the description for cleaner output.

questions.question: What should happen to commits that don't follow the conventional commit format?
choices: Place them in an 'Other Changes' section
Put them in the Features section
questions.explanation: Non-conventional commits should be included in an 'Other Changes' section. Silently skipping them means lost information; putting them in the wrong category is misleading.
